title: Organization of American States Legislative Engagement Act of 2020
official_summary:
Organization of American States Legislative Engagement Act of 2020

This bill directs the Department of State to report to Congress a strategy for supporting the anti-corruption and human rights promotion efforts of the Organization of American States (OAS), including (1) an assessment of U.S. activities with the OAS to address such matters, (2) an assessment of necessary reforms and initiatives to prioritize and reinforce OAS efforts on such matters, and (3) a detailed plan for implementing the reported strategy. The State Department shall report annually to Congress on actions taken to implement this strategy.

summary.headline: This law requires the State Department to create and report on a plan for supporting the Organization of American States on anti-corruption and human rights work.
summary.what_it_does: The law directs the Department of State to report to Congress on a strategy for supporting the Organization of American States (OAS) in fighting corruption and promoting human rights. The report must include an assessment of current U.S. work with the OAS on these issues, an assessment of reforms that could strengthen OAS efforts, and a detailed plan to carry out the strategy. The State Department must also report to Congress each year on steps taken to put the strategy into action.

who_it_affects.how: The department must prepare a strategy report, a detailed implementation plan, and annual progress reports for Congress.
They receive the strategy report and yearly updates on how the State Department is carrying out the plan.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 13, 2021, and its reporting requirements apply from that date; the summary does not give specific deadlines for the reports.
